title: Slowing Down
human_question: What actually happens in a single moment of seeing, hearing, or touching?
journey: Chathura spends time with people whose lives depend on noticing: craftspeople, fishers reading water, trackers, musicians, cooks.
surface: The pleasure of close attention: small sounds, textures, timing, the skill of seeing what others miss.
depth: The cognitive process (vīthi): 'I see' is a rapid sequence of mind-moments with no separate seer behind it. The seven universal factors present in every moment; doors, objects, bases and functions; the seventeen-moment lifespan of matter. Inside the process is a gap, impulsion (javana), where choice happens and action is made. This is the hinge of the whole series.

arc.opening: A craft or practice that demands total attention. Object 5 is acquired here.
arc.middle: Seeing, hearing, remembering and imagining, slowed down and taken apart through real work and real skill.
arc.closing: In the gap inside a moment there is a choice, and a choice can be good.

hands_off: In that gap we can choose goodness.

lesson.in_simple_terms: What feels like one simple act of seeing or hearing is, on the Abhidhamma's account, a quick relay of separate steps: something arrives, the mind turns toward it, bare colour or sound registers, it is sorted and settled, and only then comes a response. The early steps run the same way in everyone, in their own order, and many faint contacts never get past them. The response at the end is where good or harm takes shape, and this series reads that moment as a choice.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: එක් දැකීමක් හෝ ඇසීමක් පවා පිළිවෙළින් එන සිත් රැසක් වන අතර, එහි මුල් කොටස සැමට එක ලෙසම සිදු වේ. කුසල් හෝ අකුසල් හැඩ ගැසෙන්නේ අවසානයේ එන ජවන් සිත්වලය.
lesson.the_teaching: The Abhidhamma teaches that nothing a person does happens in a single mind-moment: seeing, hearing, speaking or giving each needs an ordered series, a cognitive process (vīthi), entered through one of six doors (C038, C035). The process runs through fixed functions: the resting mind is disturbed, turns toward the object, bare seeing or hearing occurs, then receiving, investigating and determining, then impulsion (javana) and registration, and seven factors such as contact, feeling and attention are present in every one of these moments (C034, C041, C020). How far the process runs depends on how strongly the object arrives, and many faint contacts never reach a response at all (C040, C045). The texts say this order runs by itself, with no doer arranging it, and they place the wholesome or unwholesome quality of a response in impulsion (C040, C043, C034). The sources never call impulsion 'choice' and never state that there is 'no separate seer'; both are the series' own framings of this teaching.
progression: EPD-0036 Seven Doors of a Leaf: experience comes in through separate doors, each taking only its own kind of object and resting on the living body.
EPD-0037 Salt That Never Stops Forming: the things the senses meet are brief and constantly replaced, which is why they look unchanged.
EPD-0038 What the Net Cannot See: most contacts are too faint or too late to become an experience; only strong ones get the full process.
EPD-0039 Only Colour, Not Yet a Flower: even a clear sight begins as bare colour; names and values are added afterwards.
EPD-0040 Turning Toward: before seeing, the mind turns toward the object without knowing it, and after sorting it settles what the thing is, still before any response.
EPD-0041 What Came Back Home: the sixth door takes past things and names; remembering a place is not meeting it as it is now.
EPD-0042 One Strike, A Thousand Echoes: one contact can set off hundreds of later mind-door processes, like a bell's fading hum.
EPD-0043 The Work Between Moments: every moment, easy or hard, carries the same seven factors, including contact, feeling, perception, volition and attention.
EPD-0044 The Score for a Vanishing Sound: no act happens in one moment; the texts chart the seventeen-moment sequence so it can be learned.
EPD-0045 The Close Call: when an object arrives late or faint the process is shorter, and decision cannot coexist with doubt.
EPD-0046 No One at the Wheel: the sequence runs by its own order with no one arranging it, yet the quality of the response depends on how the object is attended to.
EPD-0047 What's Left When It Runs Out: the neutral machinery carries no wish to act; merit or its absence is made at impulsion, which the series reads as the moment of choice.
lesson.builds_on: GRP-04 (Lost) set out doubt, restlessness and delusion as the vocabulary of being stuck, and handed on a turn: slow down and look at a single moment. This group takes that turn literally, taking one moment of experience apart to find where, beneath the confusion, a response is actually formed.
lesson.hands_to_next: If good or harm takes shape at the moment of response (the series' 'gap in which we can choose goodness'), what is a good response actually made of? GRP-06 (Kindness) takes that up: the many beautiful factors that arise together in a good mind, and how kindness becomes a practice.
